race: Formula 1 Singapore Airlines Singapore Grand Prix 2026

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: Welcome to The Race Weekend Podcast, and Singapore is ready to roar, because Max Verstappen has pole position and the street is set for chaos.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: That is the perfect headline, because Red Bull took pole ahead of the Ferraris, and the sprint already gave us a huge twist with George Russell crashing out.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: So the question is simple, how does anyone catch Max when he is carrying this much momentum into the full race on a street circuit?

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: The story is that no one is very happy at McLaren, and that is a fair read, because their Saturday was not exactly smooth in Singapore.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: And the Verstappen revival is a problem for McLaren, not necessarily for Kimi Antonelli, which is a useful way to frame the weekend.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: Ha, that is gold, but let us get to the top three, and I am starting with Max because he is the obvious pick.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: Agreed, because he has pole position, he won the sprint, and his Singapore history is solid, with an average finish of third over three races.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: But I still hear the settings issue in my head, and a small mistake on a street can turn a win into a long night.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: That is the risk, but two podiums in three races here makes me trust him, even if the traffic gets tight early.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: Now George Russell is our second pick, and I know the sprint crash hurts, but the car and the championship form are too strong to ignore.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: He starts second, he had the fastest practice, and the championship form is strong, so I can see him fighting Max right to the end.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: But his Singapore average is seventh, and only one podium in three races means I am not promising a win, just a podium fight.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: That is fair, and it makes Lewis Hamilton the perfect third pick, because Ferrari look quick from sixth and he brought the sprint second home.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: I like that, because his qualifying was strong, his best finish here is third, and his average is fifth point seven over three races.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: The question is whether he can pass Max when it matters, because that is where a Ferrari can become a race winner.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: Ha, that is the race in one line, and I am still waiting for someone to make the first big mistake.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: Before the final list, one deep cut, because car fifty five has to start from the pit lane after a Parc Fermé modification.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: That is a huge change, because the back of the grid can become a proper traffic jam with a little extra spice.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: And if you want a low confidence gamble, Isack Hadjar is tenth despite Red Bull pace, because the sprint and history worry me.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: I agree, because he starts ninth, but the sprint did not go his way, and a tricky Singapore history makes him a long shot.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: Let us keep the rest of the top ten moving, because Charles Leclerc is fourth on our list, with a third grid slot and a sprint third place.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: But he has no Singapore podium in history, so I am calling a strong points finish, not a miracle, unless Max has a bad day.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: Kimi Antonelli is fifth, and the championship leader starts seventh, so this is a street race where experience can matter a lot.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: Then Oscar Piastri is sixth, because McLaren have good Singapore history, even if the weekend has had issues and the sprint did not go their way.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: Lando Norris is seventh, with the best Singapore history in the top ten, but the McLaren struggles make me keep him just ahead of the points battle.

segments.speaker: michael
segments.text: That is a strong grid, and I am still waiting for the first mistake, so give us the full top ten in one breath.

segments.speaker: paul
segments.text: Here is our top ten: Max Verstappen, George Russell, Lewis Hamilton, Charles Leclerc, Kimi Antonelli, Oscar Piastri, Lando Norris, Liam Lawson, Pierre Gasly, and Isack Hadjar. See you in Singapore.
